newsitem.title: USA: Royal Caribbean CFO says bookings strong.
newsitem.headline: Royal Caribbean CFO says bookings strong.

text.p: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd's passenger bookings are virtually sold out through the end of March, and business is brisk for travel well through June, the company's chief financial officer said on Tuesday.
"The tone of business is terrific," CFO Richard Glasier told investors at a conference sponsored by Raymond James & Associates Inc. He also said fares were moderately higher.
Fear of overcapacity, spurred by the launch of larger passenger ships, had hung over the cruise industry for several years, Glasier said.
"We are booked in the first quarter. We're substantially booked in the second quarter. The summer is looking good," Glasier said.
Rivals, including the largest operator, Carnival Corp, were also showing strong bookings.
Fares were rising, too, he said.
"We're now seeing increases, albeit modest, at higher capacity," he said.
A year ago, during the first half of 1996, fares were being discounted, he said.
